meta.description:
Verifies a release tag cut on the commit a merge produced while the
release policies were evaluated on the pull request's head. The
subject is the **tagged commit**, what a builder checks out at the
tag, so a build at the tag can find the evaluation results and gate
on them. The tag's signed trailers are the link: the set checks the
tag is signed by the releaser, that its trailers are present and
well formed, that the evaluated commit carries a passing results
attestation signed by the releaser, and that both the tagged
commit and the evaluated commit carry the tree the tag names, so
what was released is what was evaluated. The evaluated commit is
derived from git where git can give it, a merge commit's second
parent; a squash or a rebase rewrites history, and only then is the
`Evaluated-Commit` trailer load-bearing.

The releaser is pinned by the `releaser` and `releaser_issuer`
context values, matched by the tenets against the verified
signers, so the run passes no `--signer`: a signer constraint
would wrongly apply to the git objects the chains cross, which
are proven by their hashes, not by who signed them.

The evidence comes from two collectors:
`git:https://github.com/ORG/REPO@v1.2.0` describes the tag and the
commits with their signatures verified (the evaluated commit
fetched on demand when no branch reaches it), and
`dnote:https://github.com/ORG/REPO` serves the evaluated commit's
results from its git note.
meta.name: Release Tag

meta.description:
Passes when the subject commit is the target of an annotated tag
whose signature verifies and whose signer is the releaser named
in the context: miniprow's keyless identity, for a tag it cut.

The subject is the **tagged commit**, what a builder checks out at
the tag. The tag is the releaser's claim that the release policies
passed on the evaluated commit and that the tagged commit carries
the evaluated tree; the claim is worth exactly as much as the
signature on it. The evidence is the git tag attestation
(`https://carabiner.dev/git/tag/v0`) the carabiner git collector
synthesizes from the tag object, which names both the tag and the
commit it points at as subjects; its verification is the tag's own
signature, checked by the collector: sigstore against the Fulcio
chain and the Rekor log, or PGP against the keys it holds. The
tenet requires that verification and matches its signer against
the `releaser` and `releaser_issuer` context values, so the
releaser is pinned by whoever runs the verification, not baked
into the policy, and no `--signer` constraint is needed on the
run (one would wrongly constrain the git objects the sibling
policies chain through).

## Verifying

```
ampel verify --subject-hash sha1:<tagged commit> \\
    -c git:https://github.com/ORG/REPO@v1.2.0 \\
    -p git+https://github.com/carabiner-dev/policies#release/release-tag-signed.json \\
    --context releaser:<releaser identity> \\
    --context releaser_issuer:<its OIDC issuer>
```
meta.name: Release Tag Signed by the Releaser

tenets.code:
predicates.exists(p, p.verification.verified &&
    p.verification.signers.exists(s, has(s.sigstore) &&
        s.sigstore.identity == context.releaser &&
        s.sigstore.issuer == context.releaser_issuer))

error.message: The tag is not signed by the releaser
error.guidance: The tag on this commit must carry a verified signature whose sigstore identity and issuer are the releaser's, given as the releaser and releaser_issuer context values. An unsigned tag, a PGP-signed one, or another signer is not a release by this releaser.

assessment.message: The tag is signed by the releaser

meta.description:
Passes when the subject commit is the target of an annotated tag
whose message carries the trailers a release tag needs to be
verified back to the commit the policies were evaluated on.

A release tag cut by a tagger such as miniprow lands on the commit
the merge produced, while the policies were evaluated on the pull
request's head. The tag's trailers are the signed link between the
two: `Evaluated-Commit` names the head, `Tree` the tree both
commits share, `Pull-Request` the pull request, and
`Merge-Strategy` how the head reached the branch. This policy
checks the trailers are present and well formed; the other
policies in the `release-tag` set follow them.

The subject is the tagged commit. The tag is described by a git
tag attestation (`https://carabiner.dev/git/tag/v0`), synthesized
by the carabiner git collector from the tag object with the
message's trailers parsed as git defines them, naming both the tag
object and the commit as subjects.
meta.name: Release Tag Trailers

error.message: The tag does not point at a commit
error.guidance: A release tag must point at the commit the release is cut from, not at another tag, a tree or a blob.

assessment.message: The tag points at a commit

error.message: The tag does not name the evaluated commit
error.guidance: The tag message must end with exactly one `Evaluated-Commit: <sha>` trailer naming the commit the release policies were evaluated on, as a full 40-character sha.

assessment.message: The tag names the commit the policies were evaluated on

error.message: The tag does not name the released tree
error.guidance: The tag message must end with exactly one `Tree: <sha>` trailer naming the tree both the tagged commit and the evaluated commit carry.

assessment.message: The tag names the tree the tagged and the evaluated commits share

error.message: The tag does not name the pull request
error.guidance: The tag message must end with exactly one `Pull-Request: <number>` trailer. A squashed or rebased head is only reachable through the pull request's ref, so a verifier needs the number.

assessment.message: The tag names the pull request the release came from

error.message: The tag does not state a known merge strategy
error.guidance: The tag message must end with a `Merge-Strategy: merge|squash|rebase` trailer.

assessment.message: The tag states how the evaluated commit reached the branch

meta.description:
Passes when the commit the release policies were evaluated on, the
pull request's head, carries an AMPEL results attestation whose
verdict is PASS, signed by the releaser.

The subject is the tagged commit; the evaluation results live on
the head. The policy reaches the head through git wherever git can
give it: for a merge commit the evaluated head is the merge's
second parent, read from the tagged commit's own attestation
(`https://carabiner.dev/git/commit/v0`). A squash or a rebase
rewrites history and leaves no link, so for those the chain reads
the tag's `Evaluated-Commit` trailer, the one place the trailer
is load-bearing. `Merge-Strategy` says which path applies. The
tenet then reads the results attestation
(`https://carabiner.dev/ampel/resultset/v0`) the releaser stored
for the head and requires a PASS verdict signed by the releaser
named in the `releaser` and `releaser_issuer` context values.
The head may no longer be on any branch, so the collectors must
reach it: the git collector fetches it on demand, the dynamic note
collector serves its note by sha.
meta.name: Release Policies Passed on the Evaluated Commit

tenets.code:
predicates.exists(p, p.data.status == "PASS" && size(p.data.results) > 0 &&
    p.verification.verified &&
    p.verification.signers.exists(s, has(s.sigstore) &&
        s.sigstore.identity == context.releaser &&
        s.sigstore.issuer == context.releaser_issuer))

error.message: No passing results attestation from the releaser for the evaluated commit
error.guidance: The commit the release policies were evaluated on must carry a results attestation with at least one result and a PASS verdict, signed by the releaser given as the releaser and releaser_issuer context values.

assessment.message: The release policies passed on the evaluated commit, as the releaser recorded

meta.description:
Passes when the subject commit, the one the release tag points at,
carries the tree the tag's `Tree` trailer names.

A release tag lands on the commit a merge produced while the
policies were evaluated on the pull request's head; what makes
the tag honest is that both commits carry the same tree. The tag
names that tree in its signed `Tree` trailer. Both the tag
attestation (`https://carabiner.dev/git/tag/v0`) and the commit's
own attestation (`https://carabiner.dev/git/commit/v0`, synthesized
from the commit object) are evidence about the subject, so the
tenet compares them directly. Its sibling
`release-evaluated-commit-tree` does the same for the evaluated
commit; together they establish the two trees are one.
meta.name: Tagged Commit Carries the Named Tree

tenets.code:
predicates.exists(t, t.predicate_type == "https://carabiner.dev/git/tag/v0" &&
    predicates.exists(c, c.predicate_type == "https://carabiner.dev/git/commit/v0" &&
        c.data.tree == t.data.trailers["Tree"][0]))

error.message: The tagged commit does not carry the tree the tag names
error.guidance: The release tag's Tree trailer must name the tagged commit's tree. A tag whose target carries another tree was cut on content the policies never saw.

assessment.message: The tagged commit carries the tree the tag names

meta.description:
Passes when the commit the release policies were evaluated on
carries the tree the tag's `Tree` trailer names.

The subject is the tagged commit. The evaluated commit is reached
as `release-evaluated-commit-passed` reaches it: the merge's
second parent for a merge commit, the `Evaluated-Commit` trailer
for a squash or a rebase. Its tree, read from its attestation
(`https://carabiner.dev/git/commit/v0`), must be the one the tag
names. With `release-tagged-commit-tree` this establishes that
the tagged commit and the evaluated commit carry the same tree:
what was released is what was evaluated.
meta.name: Evaluated Commit Carries the Named Tree

error.message: The evaluated commit does not carry the tree the tag names
error.guidance: The release tag's Tree trailer must name the evaluated commit's tree, the content the policies passed on.

assessment.message: The evaluated commit carries the tree the tag names
